value.rationale: The degree-two simplex is the smallest complete nonrectangular triangular two-dimensional spectral aperture and appears as a canonical configuration in polyphase sparse-array analysis. Its sixth moment probes cubic convolution and higher-order aggregate spectral peaks rather than the fourth-moment autocorrelation energy. The exact low-alphabet benchmark exhibits a genuine nonnested phase-resolution diagram, an algebraic pentaphase optimum, symmetry breaking at q=5, and a certified continuous-phase improvement; such precise benchmarks and optimizer classes are useful for design and comparison. The result deliberately does not claim an unrestricted continuous optimum or downstream theorem.
